dict.string: Walnut shows your calendar events alongside tasks in the calendar view. Events are read-only and never leave your device.
Walnut uses the camera to scan the pairing QR code from your Walnut console and to take photos you attach to chats and notes.

Walnut reads the Apple Health data you allow, so your AI can answer questions about your sleep, activity, heart and more. It goes only to your own Walnut server, on your Mac or on a cloud machine you run, and from there to the AI provider that server uses.
Only Walnut's test builds add sample health data, to check that syncing works. The App Store version never changes your Apple Health data.
Walnut connects straight to your Walnut on this Wi-Fi network when it can, which is faster than going through the cloud.

With Places on, Walnut records the places you visit, even while it is closed, so your AI can answer where you were. They go only to your own Walnut server, on your Mac or on a cloud machine you run, and from there to the AI provider that server uses. Apple Maps names each place. iOS records visits only with Always.

Walnut uses your location only for Places, after you turn it on. The places you visit go only to your own Walnut server, on your Mac or on a cloud machine you run, and from there to the AI provider that server uses. Apple Maps names each place.

Walnut uses the microphone for voice input. Your recording goes only to your own Walnut server, on your Mac or on a cloud machine you run, which turns it into text itself or with a speech service you set up on it.
Record and send to your AI
